title: ERAN recording order - the 220 board, most valuable first
measured_on: 657 wavs in D:/CLAUDE/eran-brain/booth/staged/t06, through the frozen cochlea (body/ears.py, repr=cochlea, 24 bands x 8 slices = 192 dims, EAR_FROZEN=True), with verify.py's probe (1-NN, z-scored by TRAIN mu/sd, squared euclidean)
rule: Every session starts again at rank 1 and walks down. A unit is DONE when it has 12 takes spread over 3 different days; done units are skipped. Stopping is allowed after any single unit.

measured_basis.consonant_crowding: cos of the z-scored cochlea prototype to the nearest OTHER consonant, 20 sounds x 3 takes

twenty_way_probe.caveat: leave-one-take-out over 3 BACK-TO-BACK takes: an optimistic split, and duration alone already reaches 0.20, so part of this is clip length, not timbre. Used for RANKING only, never as an accuracy claim.

prototype_error.note: per-dim on z-scored cochlea vectors; sittings = runs separated by >120 s; the only units with >=2 sittings are ah, ih, ma

units.why: ROW 1 - /a/. All 25 units ever recorded are a consonant+/a/ or an /a/-word, so this is the only row where a 20-way consonant test can be built at all. Its present data is 3 back-to-back takes from ONE sitting on 2026-08-23 - the leakiest split there is. Consonants are the ear's weak axis: 63-77% on the /a/-family consonant pairs against 92.3-100.0% on vowel pairs, same design, chance 50%. And ABBA is /a/.  ||  Milestone anchor: both ABBA and IMA open on this sound. Measured crowding 0.3857 (nearest: pe).

This row is where that question gets answered, after the 140 real sounds are in.
